items.title: Static stretching before exercise
items.claim: Sports science guidance on pre-exercise static stretching changed substantially. What do current consensus reviews say?

options.text: Static stretching pre-exercise reliably reduces injury and improves performance
Long static holds before power activities can reduce subsequent performance; dynamic warm-up is generally preferred
No warm-up of any kind is recommended

items.reveal_title: Pre-exercise long static holds can hurt power output
items.reveal:
Reviews (Behm and Chaouachi, 2011; Behm et al., 2016) summarise that holds longer than around 60 seconds before sprint or jump activities can transiently reduce performance.

Dynamic warm-ups are now standard in elite team-sport protocols.
items.why: Practice guidelines often persist in coaching long after research has moved on.

items.title: First modern Olympics
items.claim: Approximately how many athletes competed at the first modern Olympics in Athens 1896?
items.reveal:
Sources vary from around 241 to 280 athletes from roughly 14 nations.

Women first competed at Paris 1900 (in tennis, golf and a few other sports).
items.why: The scale of contemporary Olympics is not built in; it grew from a modest revival.

items.title: Title IX participation increase
items.claim: Title IX of the US Education Amendments (1972) banned sex discrimination in federally funded education, including athletics. By 2018, what proportion of US high school athletes were girls compared with 1971?

options.text: Roughly 10x more (about 295,000 in 1971 versus over 3 million by the 2010s)

items.reveal:
National Federation of State High School Associations data show girls' high school athletic participation rising from around 295,000 in 1971-72 to over 3.4 million in 2018-19.

Funding and facility disparities persist; the legal framework changed participation faster than parity.
items.why: Single policy interventions can reshape participation across decades.
